title: Fallen Scots pine trunk section — forest/forest-steppe landscape prop
era: natural (Ukrainian/Russian forest-steppe and pine bor landscape)

sources.scots_pine_wiki: Pinus sylvestris — Wikipedia: 'mature 25–35 m (exceptionally >45 m), trunk to ~1 m diameter, orange-brown upper bark; foundation species on poor dry sandy sites'
sources.scots_pine_jrc: EU JRC Forest Atlas via research brief: 'trunk diameter range 0.5–1.3 m (exceptionally >1.7 m)'
sources.bark_texture_conifers: conifers.org + Wikipedia — 'Scots pine bark is TWO-TONE (signature): lower trunk thick scaly grey-brown deeply fissured plates up to ~5 cm thick; upper trunk + branches thin flaking orange-red/copper'
sources.bor_ground_layer: EUNIS habitat 1283; Kytöviita 2009, Functional Ecology — зеленомошник type = deep-green Pleurozium moss ground layer characteristic of nutrient-poor acidic late-successional pine forest; fallen logs in this biome accumulate damp Pleurozium on ground-contact surface
sources.research_brief: Ecology + visual character of Ukrainian/Russian regional landscape biomes — ENGENDROS PURGE world plan + model dossiers (2026-06-10)

trunk_dims.note: 0.50 m diameter = lower bound of the sourced 0.5–1.3 m DBH range (EU JRC/Wikipedia); a younger-to-mid-age mature specimen appropriate for a forest-steppe prop; using this as the butt-end radius (widest end)

taper.note: UNSOURCED specific taper rate — typical pine trunk taper is in the range 1–2 cm/m but no field measurement cited. 30 mm taper over 2.4 m section (~1.25 cm/m) is mid-range plausible. Flagged in needs[]

bark_texture.bark_type: two-tone: lower = thick scaly grey-brown deeply fissured plates (up to ~50 mm); upper/exposed = thin flaking orange-red/copper
bark_texture.note: Bark thickness stated as 'up to ~5 cm' — using 40 mm as nominal lower-trunk value; precise mean not sourced → needs[]

log_length.note: DESIGN VALUE — no field or forestry standard sourced for a prop log section length. 2.4 m chosen as FPS-scale obstacle: climbable/crouchable cover at ~1.5–1.6× player height. Flagged in needs[]

moss_feature.desc: Pleurozium schreberi (зеленомошник) deep-green moss accumulates on the ground-contact face of fallen logs in pine bor biome
moss_feature.note: Presence sourced; exact coverage dimensions are a design estimate from trunk footprint

derivation.derivation: shadow_band h = ~0.5 × diameter (120/500=24%); hi_strip h = ~12% diameter; bark ridges w = bark_thickness; end_grain r = trunk_radius - bark_thickness (250-40=210 trimmed to 190 for visible ring gap); root_bulge slightly wider than trunk (480 vs 500 mm diameter); knot = proportional scar; moss patch covers ~50% of bottom arc width × 62% of log length

main_body.desc: Tapered cylinder, butt end wider, top end narrower

bottom_shadow.desc: Dark lower bark zone: old grey-brown scaly plates + ground-shadow darkening

top_highlight.desc: Lighter sunlit strip along the top of the log: exposed thin upper orange-copper bark layer

bark_ridges_lr.desc: Longitudinal bark plate ridges on left/right flanks — the fissured grey-brown lower-bark texture

end_grain.desc: Pale exposed heartwood at the cut/broken end, circular face showing raw wood

root_bulge.desc: Slight flare/bulge at the wider butt end — root collar and soil flare

knot.desc: Dark old branch-knot scar on the flank — a circular dark recess in the bark

moss.desc: Damp green moss (Pleurozium) on the ground-contact underside

game_model_purpose: World prop — horizontal obstacle/cover piece in forest-steppe and pine bor biomes; climbable/crouchable cover at FPS human scale; can be scattered as environmental debris or placed near treelines/shelterbelts
needs: Specific Scots pine trunk taper rate (cm/m) from a forestry or silviculture reference — current taper (r=0.25 m → r=0.22 m over 2.4 m) is a design estimate
Precise lower-bark thickness for Scots pine: 'up to ~5 cm' is the stated maximum; mean/typical value not sourced
Standard or common log-section length for a fallen forest obstacle — current 2.4 m is a game-design value with no field or forestry source
